AFTER THE FACT -- why division cannot fake a cell-cycle call, in one number
(i) DIVISION IS NOT COMMON-MODE -- I assumed it was and the data says no.
Over 4,821 genes with half-lives from 0.50 h to 5764 h,
the division-only six-window amplitude runs 1.0882 to 1.7697, a
62.6% spread, and it tracks half-life: a 30-minute protein re-equilibrates
right after halving and barely registers; a stable one carries the whole sawtooth.
So division does create differential amplitude between genes.
(ii) LOOP 123 SURVIVES FOR A STRONGER REASON: THE CEILING IS ANALYTIC.
P(T-) = 2*P(0+) exactly, for every b, confirmed to 1.3e-11 in D1. Averaged into six
windows that becomes 1.7698, and that is a HARD upper bound -- no half-life,
no synthesis rate, no parameter can push bare division past it. Loop 123's threshold
is 2.0. The margin is 1.130x, thin but guaranteed rather than
empirical, and D4 confirmed 0 of 4,821 genes reach it.
Its 866 two-fold proteins are not division artefacts. The correction I came here
expecting to make is not needed -- for a reason I had to be shown.
(iii) AND THE MEASUREMENT IS ALREADY MOSTLY DIVISION-CORRECTED.
D5: LFQ leaves a 10.82% trend in the median gene against the 77.0% a
per-cell quantification would show -- about 86% divided out. Consistent with D4's
finding that division-only amplitude (1.758) EXCEEDS what Ly measured
(1.307) for 87% of genes: the sawtooth is largely gone from the data
before anyone analysed it. D5 failed a gate I set at 10%, missing by
0.82%. A real residual, reported as one.
(iv) WHAT DIVISION DOES CHANGE, measured rather than asserted:
- every rate in this model is understated by at most 3.97%, now proved
rather than assumed (D2), with the worst case at the most stable proteins
- mRNA carries a 24.0% partitioning noise floor from division alone,
protein only 0.48% -- a 49-fold difference that comes entirely
from copy number, and it means single-cell mRNA noise has an irreducible
component this model can now compute without fitting anything
